# curl / fuzz_bufq

curl's own fuzz target `fuzz_bufq` ([source](source/fuzz_bufq.cc), modified; see below), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over curl (curl/curl at f190aa8e).

Runs a fuzzer-chosen sequence of operations on one curl byte queue (bufq) and checks it with 12 asserts (listed below): the bytes read, peeked and passed follow the 0..255 pattern written, the queue's length and emptiness match the harness's byte count before each operation, and the count stays within the capacity after each write, slurp and sipn.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against curl at commit f190aa8e.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified for these builds. source/fuzz_bufq.cc is curl-fuzzer 4768d8de's fuzz_bufq.cc with projects/curl/fuzz_bufq/proofs/provenance/recipe/targets/curl-fuzz_bufq/fuzz_bufq-no-syscalls.patch applied; source/fuzz_bufq.h is unmodified.
- The patch makes the harness's template buffer a constant table in read-only data, built at compile time, in place of the mmap(MAP_SHARED) and mprotect(PROT_READ) buffer its first call made, and removes its signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN).

## What the harness checks
- Each piece Curl_bufq_pass hands its writer callback, up to the bytes the pass still asks for, follows the 0..255 pattern from the next byte to read (upstream line 94). The pattern repeats every 256 bytes ([line 100](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L100)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Before each operation, Curl_bufq_is_empty is true exactly when the harness's count of queued bytes is 0 (upstream line 169) ([line 175](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L175)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Before each operation, Curl_bufq_len equals the harness's count of queued bytes (upstream line 170) ([line 176](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L176)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- The bytes Curl_bufq_peek returns follow the pattern from the next byte to read (upstream line 188). The pattern repeats every 256 bytes ([line 194](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L194)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- The bytes Curl_bufq_peek_at returns at an offset follow the pattern from that offset (upstream line 203). The pattern repeats every 256 bytes ([line 209](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L209)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Always true: buffer_bytes >= 0 after a read, where buffer_bytes is a size_t (upstream line 219). The compiler removes it: its text is in none of the four binaries. No change to curl can make it fail ([line 225](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L225)): assert(); compiled out.
- The bytes Curl_bufq_read copies out follow the pattern from the next byte to read (upstream line 222). The pattern repeats every 256 bytes ([line 228](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L228)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- After Curl_bufq_slurp, the harness's count of queued bytes is at most chunk_size * max_chunks (upstream line 244) ([line 250](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L250)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- After a successful Curl_bufq_sipn, the count is at most chunk_size * max_chunks (upstream line 258) ([line 264](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L264)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Always true: buffer_bytes >= 0 after a pass, where buffer_bytes is a size_t (upstream line 280). The compiler removes it: its text is in none of the four binaries. No change to curl can make it fail ([line 286](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L286)): assert(); compiled out.
- After a successful Curl_bufq_write, the count is at most chunk_size * max_chunks (upstream line 305) ([line 311](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L311)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Never reached: assert(false) in the switch default (upstream line 314), but op_type is in 0..8 and each value has a case. The plain and ASan builds drop it; the UBSan and ASan+UBSan builds keep it, so it is neither live nor compiled out in all four. No change to curl can make it fail ([line 320](source/fuzz_bufq.cc#L320)): assert(); not confirmed in the binary.

A failure of any of the checks at line 100, line 175, line 176, line 194, line 209, line 228, line 250, line 264 and line 311 ends the process with a status that the halts statements below that name them exclude, so a proof of one of those statements implies them on every input it covers. No statement here proves the other checks.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v), [Characterise.v](Characterise.v), [Distribution.v](Distribution.v))

| statement | in one line | status |
|---|---|---|
| `plain_halts` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at line 100, line 175, line 176, line 194, line 209, line 228, line 250, line 264 and line 311 above hold | open |
| `ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at line 100, line 175, line 176, line 194, line 209, line 228, line 250, line 264 and line 311 above hold | open |
| `asan_halts` | on every input on which the ASan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at line 100, line 175, line 176, line 194, line 209, line 228, line 250, line 264 and line 311 above hold | open |
| `asan_ubsan_halts` | on every input on which the ASan+UBSan build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise), it exits with status 0 or 2; so the checks at line 100, line 175, line 176, line 194, line 209, line 228, line 250, line 264 and line 311 above hold | open |
| `asan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan never fires; abort read as SIGABRT | open |
| `ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; UBSan never fires; abort read as SIGABRT | open |
| `asan_ubsan_agrees` | on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding 2 GiB (a premise): neither build reaches an error and both have the same set of observable behaviours; ASan+UBSan never fires; abort read as SIGABRT | open |
| `asan_disagrees_at_most` | P[plain and ASan disagree] <= b under [Distribution.v](Distribution.v) | open (best proved b: none) |
| `ubsan_disagrees_at_most` | P[plain and UBSan disagree] <= b under [Distribution.v](Distribution.v) | open (best proved b: none) |
| `asan_ubsan_disagrees_at_most` | P[plain and ASan+UBSan disagree] <= b under [Distribution.v](Distribution.v) | open (best proved b: none) |
| `asan_agreement_decidable` | some program decides exactly the inputs where plain and ASan agree | open |
| `ubsan_agreement_decidable` | some program decides exactly the inputs where plain and UBSan agree | open |
| `asan_ubsan_agreement_decidable` | some program decides exactly the inputs where plain and ASan+UBSan agree | open |

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch curl` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `fuzz_bufq.plain` | 317,888 | `042d5bb0014e3f2f3460f1d640e599ece0d8d844681aaf537b8b7db2361385c4` |
| ubsan | `fuzz_bufq.ubsan` | 317,928 | `ab8a9b5886e5e6221c414d5a7eb8fcb974f2acd6bc5f2df937a1fe75c3564899` |
| asan | `fuzz_bufq.asan` | 1,093,368 | `787dbd38da8e23b964a94193cba299461a8eae36c30aa343b9aa7fe32908d625` |
| asan-ubsan | `fuzz_bufq.asan-ubsan` | 1,090,584 | `25ccbd40e13c021e6c9f2d9e343bf8f54ab26f84b9c9258a36b77973d946ff37` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
